citations.S1: builds SQL by string interpolation from request-controlled `user_id`/`status`
citations.S2: `get_user_orders` opens a `sqlite3.connect` and never closes it (no `close()`, no context manager, no `try/finally`)
citations.S3: `order[0]` is the `id` column, an int, not a str. `str + int` raises `TypeError`
citations.S5: Float arithmetic on currency accumulates rounding error and can misprice orders
citations.S6: A negative `pct` increases the price; `pct > 100` gives a negative amount. Neither is checked.
citations.S7: allowlist known statuses and raise on anything else
citations.S8: nothing verifies the caller is allowed to see `user_id`'s orders — `user_id` comes straight from the request
citations.S11: propagates a raw `sqlite3` exception ... straight to the caller with no context
citations.S13: No `LIMIT` on the query — a user with a huge order history returns everything into memory in one `fetchall()`
